title: Quick and reliable method for retina dissociation and separation of rod photoreceptor perikarya from adult mice
author: Feodorova, Koch, et al.
materials: -Add 32 ml Earle’s balanced salt solution (EBSS) to Vial 4 (ovomucoid). When everything is thoroughly dissolved, aliquot the solution into 2 ml screw cap tubes, labeled as “tube 4” and store them at +4 °C.-Add 5 ml EBSS to Vial 2 (papain) and incubate at 37 °C until the solution becomes clear (approx. 10 min).-Add 500 μl EBSS to Vial 3 (DNase) and gently invert the vial several times to dissolve the DNase; avoid vigorous mixing.-Add 250 μl of DNase to Vial 2 (papain).-Aliquot the papain solution into 250 μl aliquots in 2 ml screw cap tubes, labeled as “tube 1”, and store the tubes at −20 °C.-Aliquot the DNase solution into 15 μl aliquots in 1.5 ml screw cap tubes, labeled as “tube 2”, and store the tubes at −20 °C.-Prepare 1.5 ml tubes which contain 130 μl EBSS and 15 μl ovomucoid, label them as “tube 3”, and store the tubes at +4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare enzyme stock solutions
steps.instruction: In the cell‑culture hood, make the following solutions, aliquot, and store as indicated:

substeps.instruction: Add 32 ml Earle’s balanced salt solution (EBSS) to Vial 4 containing ovomucoid, dissolve, aliquot 2 ml into screw‑cap tubes, label “tube 4”, store at +4 °C.
Add 5 ml EBSS to Vial 2 containing papain, incubate at 37 °C until clear (≈10 min).
Add 500 µl EBSS to Vial 3 containing DNase, gently invert several times to dissolve (avoid vigorous mixing).
Add 250 µl of the DNase solution to Vial 2 (papain mixture).
Aliquot the papain‑DNase mixture into 250 µl portions in 2 ml screw‑cap tubes, label “tube 1”, store at –20 °C.
Aliquot the DNase solution into 15 µl portions in 1.5 ml screw‑cap tubes, label “tube 2”, store at –20 °C.
Prepare 1.5 ml tubes containing 130 µl EBSS + 15 µl ovomucoid, label “tube 3”, store at +4 °C.

steps.title: Isolate and transfer retinas
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice and dissect retinas, then move them to the digestion tube prepared earlier.

substeps.instruction: Kill mice by cervical dislocation (protocol approved by the Animal Ethic Committee, University of Munich).
Displace the eyeball forward with a curved Dumont forceps placed around the posterior part.
Cut the cornea with a sharp blade or scalpel.
Squeeze the retina, residual pigment epithelium, and lens through the corneal cut using gentle pressure with the Dumont forceps.
Place the dissected retina in cooled PBS, remove non‑retinal tissue with forceps, and immediately transfer the retina to the digestion tube (see “tube 1” or “tube 2” as appropriate).

steps.title: Microscopic quality control (phase contrast)
steps.instruction: Assess dissociation efficiency and rod purity by phase‑contrast microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Mix a few microliters of the cell suspension with approximately 50 µl PBS.
Place the mixture on a microscope slide, cover with a coverslip, and examine immediately using a phase‑contrast microscope with a 20× objective.

steps.title: DAPI staining on polylysine‑coated slides
steps.instruction: Coat slides, attach perikarya, fix, stain nuclei with DAPI, and mount for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Mark a ~18 × 18 mm area on the back of a microscope slide with a diamond pencil.
Add 100 µl of 1 mg ml⁻¹ polylysine to the marked area, incubate 15 min, wash with ddH₂O, air‑dry; slides can be stored at +4 °C for a few days.
Add 100 µl of the perikarya suspension to the same area, incubate 15 min at room temperature (RT).
Briefly rinse the slide in PBS, fix with 4 % formaldehyde for 10 min at RT, then wash with PBS three times for 5 min each at RT.
Counterstain nuclei with 0.05 µg ml⁻¹ DAPI for 5 min at RT.
Mount cells under a coverslip using Vectashield mounting medium and seal the edges with nail polish.

steps.title: Immunostaining of perikarya
steps.instruction: Perform antibody labeling on perikarya attached to polylysine‑coated slides, followed by DAPI counterstaining and mounting.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the first four substeps of the DAPI protocol (polylysine coating, perikarya loading, PBS rinse, fixation).
Dilute primary and secondary antibodies in blocking solution.
Apply the antibody solution to the slide area with attached cells under a coverslip and incubate 45 min at RT.
Wash three times with PBST for 5 min each after each antibody incubation.
Add 0.05 µg ml⁻¹ DAPI for nuclear counterstaining (incubate as in the DAPI step).
Mount the cells under a coverslip in Vectashield mounting medium and seal with nail polish.

description: Effectiveness of cell dissociation, rod purity after sorting and rod perikarya preservation can be easily controlled microscopically at every step using either phase contrast or fluorescence microscopy. For the phase contrast microscopy, mix a few microliters of the cell suspension with approx. 50 μl of PBS, place it on a microscopic slide under a coverslip, and immediately study under phase contrast microscope equipped with 20× objective (not shown). More detailed information about sorted rods can be obtained after staining nuclei with DAPI. This requires a robust attachment of cells to a microscopic slide which is achieved by a short incubation of cells on slides coated by polylysine. Mouse rod nuclei have a very characteristic morphology and DAPI staining is sufficient for their identification and estimation of their concentration and purity. First of all, rod nuclei are the smallest nuclei in the retina (approx. 5 μm in diameter). Second, rod nuclei possess a very regular concentric arrangement of chromatin classes differentially stained by DAPI: (1) the most centrally positioned chromocenter, consisting of AT-rich major satellite repeat, is very brightly stained; (2) the central chromocenter is surrounded by a shell of less stained heterochromatin; (3) and the most peripheral rod nuclear layer consists of weakly stained GC-rich euchromatin (Fig. 2A and B). For robust identification of the sorted rod perikarya, one can also use immunostaining of rhodopsin. Since rhodopsin molecules are not very abundant in rod perikarya, the anti-rhodopsin antibody marks sparsely the adult cell bodies (Fig. 2C). For better differentiation of concentric chromatin layers in rod nuclei, one can use markers of eu- and heterochromatin. Thus, the peripheral euchromatin shell in rod nuclei can be highlighted by antibodies against histone modifications characteristic of transcriptionally active chromatin, such as H3K4me3, H3K36me3, and a number of acetylated modifications, e.g., H3K27ac
